rawCommits.subject: feat(invite): add invite friends modal and taskbar button
rawCommits.body:
Invite button in bottom left with pulse animation opens a modal
showing the user's invite code (click to copy) and referral bonus
details. Uses existing invite code store.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: add invite friends modal and taskbar button

rawCommits.subject: feat(theme): border main panels and add separate border tokens for panels vs chrome
rawCommits.body:
Adds a 1px border around the three desktop lanes (sidebar, main panel,
sidekick) so they read as discrete surfaces like the taskbar pills.
Introduces `--color-border-main-panel` and `--color-border-chrome` (both
defaulting to `--color-border`) and exposes them in Settings > Appearance
> Custom colors so users can tint the lane borders independently from
the topbar / bottom-taskbar pills. Lane borders are suppressed in
desktop wallpaper mode to keep the background clean.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: border main panels and add separate border tokens for panels vs chrome

rawCommits.subject: fix(release): reconcile release assets so a dropped upload no longer fails the pipeline
rawCommits.body:
softprops/action-gh-release@v2 occasionally surfaces "Error: other side
closed" (also EPIPE / ECONNRESET) when GitHub's upload API closes one
of its parallel asset streams mid-flight, failing the entire 40+ minute
release job even though every other asset uploaded fine.

Add infra/scripts/release/upload-release-assets-with-retry.sh, which
diffs the local artifact set against the published release, re-uploads
only the missing or wrong-sized assets via `gh release upload --clobber`
with retry on the known transient patterns, and fails the step only if
verification still shows a gap. Wire it after every softprops invocation
(immutable nightly + nightly alias, stable, mobile-nightly) with
continue-on-error so the reconciler becomes the authoritative gate.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: reconcile release assets so a dropped upload no longer fails the pipeline

rawCommits.subject: feat(desktop-shell): round panel corners and drop inset sidekick divider
rawCommits.body:
Replace the `box-shadow: inset -1px 0 0 0 var(--color-border)` divider
that the main panel host used to draw against the sidekick with explicit
border-radius corners on the sidebar (left), sidekick lane (right), and
main panel host (right, only when the sidekick is collapsed). The new
`mainPanelHostNoSidekick` modifier is composed with `cn` from @cypher-asi/zui
so the corner rounding follows the sidekick visibility state, and the
DesktopShell test asserts the modifier is absent whenever the sidekick is
mounted.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: round panel corners and drop inset sidekick divider

rawCommits.subject: feat(desktop-shell): unify sidekick width across all apps
rawCommits.body:
The sidekick lane now uses a single shared width that stays identical
when switching between apps. Per-app width persistence and the
`useSidekickWidthRetargeting` effect that resized the lane on every app
change have been removed. Width is read once at mount, persisted under
a single `aura-sidekick-width` localStorage key, and migrated from the
legacy shared / projects / per-app entries on first load so existing
users keep their preferred size.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: unify sidekick width across all apps

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): only show prompt suggestions during onboarding
rawCommits.body:
Gate the empty-thread chip row on the onboarding-store
`send_message` task so it disappears the moment the user sends
their first message ever. Subsequent empty chats no longer
display the suggestions.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: only show prompt suggestions during onboarding

rawCommits.subject: fix(desktop): self-heal corrupt settings store and surface fatal startup failures
rawCommits.body:
The published Windows installer was silently failing to launch on
upgraded machines. Symptom: double-click AURA, the harness sidecar
(aura-node-...) appears as a Background process in Task Manager,
and then nothing — no window, no error dialog, no notification.
Only `<localdata>/aura/crash.log` showed evidence of what happened:

  panicked at apps/aura-os-desktop/src/main.rs:106:10:
  server thread failed before becoming ready: RecvError

Root cause is a chain of three bugs that combine into "exits
silently with no UI":

1. `<localdata>/aura/store/settings.json` was a 1.1 MB file of
   pure NUL bytes — a torn-write artifact from a prior crash.
   `SettingsStore::load_cf` handed the bytes to
   `serde_json::from_str`, which propagated `expected value at
   line 1 column 1` straight up. The same store path is read in
   two places: `init_script::load_bootstrapped_auth_literals`
   already swallowed the error and warned, but the
   server-thread path inside `aura-os-desktop` `.expect(...)`'d
   on it and panicked.
2. `persist_cf` wrote the tmp file with `fs::write` and renamed
   it without `sync_all`. NTFS happily renames a file whose
   contents the OS has not yet flushed; a power loss or hard
   kill in that window leaves the destination as the right
   length but full of NUL bytes, which is exactly the input
   that bug 1 chokes on the next time around.
3. The release Windows binary is built with
   `windows_subsystem = "windows"`, so the panic's `eprintln!`
   went to a stderr that has no console. The only surviving
   evidence was `crash.log`, which a non-developer user has no
   reason to look at.

Fixes:

- `crates/aura-os-store/src/store.rs::load_cf`: on
  `serde_json::from_str` failure, rename the bad file aside
  to `<cf>.json.corrupt-<unix_ts>`, log a WARN, and return an
  empty CF. Mirrors the per-entry tolerance the same function
  already applies to invalid base64. Two new integration tests
  cover the all-NUL and garbage-JSON shapes.
- `crates/aura-os-store/src/store.rs::persist_cf`: replace
  `fs::write` with `OpenOptions::open` + `write_all` + a
  `sync_all` before the rename so the atomic-rename promise
  actually holds across crashes. Costs one fsync per persist.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/net/server.rs::spawn_server`:
  change the ready channel from `()` to `Result<(), String>`
  and stop `.expect`ing on `build_app_state` /
  `TcpListener::from_std`. On failure, log the error and send
  `Err(message)` back so the main thread can react.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/main.rs`: handle the new ready
  result. On `Ok(Err(_))` or `RecvError`, call a new
  `init::fatal_dialog::show_fatal_startup_failure` helper
  before exiting non-zero.
- `apps/aura-os-desktop/src/init/fatal_dialog.rs` (new): pop
  a native MessageBoxW with MB_TOPMOST + MB_SETFOREGROUND on
  Windows; fall back to `eprintln!` on macOS / Linux. The
  dialog body names the data dir, the path of the crash log,
  and the corrupt settings file the user can rename to recover.

Verified locally: `cargo test -p aura-os-store` (7 tests, both
new self-heal cases included) and
`cargo run -p aura-os-desktop -- --print-channel` (Channel CI
gate from f64e07753 still passes).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: self-heal corrupt settings store and surface fatal startup failures

rendered.title: Invite flow, desktop shell polish, and a Windows startup rescue
rendered.intro: A busy nightly: a new invite-a-friend entry point landed in the taskbar, the desktop shell got a coherent visual pass around panel borders, corners, and a single shared sidekick width, and the Windows app picked up a self-healing fix for the silent-launch failure some upgraders were hitting. Release infrastructure also got tougher against flaky GitHub asset uploads.

entries.title: Invite friends modal in the bottom taskbar
entries.summary: A pulsing invite button now lives in the bottom-left of the taskbar and opens a modal with the user's referral code and bonus details.

items.text: Added an invite entry point in the bottom taskbar with a subtle pulse animation that opens a new modal showing a click-to-copy invite code and referral bonus details, wired through the existing invite code store and UI modal store.

entries.title: Tintable borders around the desktop lanes
entries.summary: The sidebar, main panel, and sidekick now read as distinct surfaces with their own border token, separate from the topbar and taskbar chrome.

items.text: Added a 1px border around the three desktop lanes so they read as discrete surfaces like the taskbar pills, with lane borders automatically suppressed in desktop wallpaper mode.

Introduced separate `--color-border-main-panel` and `--color-border-chrome` tokens and exposed them in Settings → Appearance → Custom colors so panel borders can be tinted independently from the topbar and bottom-taskbar pills.

entries.title: Release pipeline survives dropped GitHub asset uploads
entries.summary: Nightly, stable, and mobile-nightly release jobs no longer fail outright when GitHub's upload API drops a parallel asset stream mid-flight.

items.text: Added a reconciliation script that diffs local artifacts against the published release and re-uploads only missing or wrong-sized assets with `gh release upload --clobber`, retrying on the known transient errors (`other side closed`, EPIPE, ECONNRESET) and failing only if a real gap remains.

Wired the reconciler after every softprops/action-gh-release@v2 step across the nightly, nightly alias, stable, and mobile-nightly workflows with continue-on-error, so a flaky upload no longer wastes a 40+ minute release run.

entries.title: Rounded panels, one sidekick width, and onboarding-only prompt chips
entries.summary: The desktop shell swapped its inset sidekick divider for rounded panel corners, collapsed per-app sidekick widths down to a single shared value, and stopped showing prompt suggestions to returning users.

items.text: Replaced the inset shadow that separated the main panel from the sidekick with explicit rounded corners on the sidebar, sidekick lane, and (when the sidekick is collapsed) the main panel host, driven by a new visibility-aware modifier.

Unified the sidekick lane to a single shared width across every app, persisted under one `aura-sidekick-width` key and migrated from the legacy shared, projects, and per-app entries so existing users keep their preferred size.

Prompt suggestion chips on empty chats are now gated on the onboarding `send_message` task, so they disappear the moment a user sends their first message ever and don't reappear in later empty threads.

entries.title: Windows startup recovers from a corrupt settings file
entries.summary: The Desktop app no longer vanishes silently when `settings.json` has been torn-written to NUL bytes, and it now shows a clear failure dialog instead of exiting without any UI.

items.text: The settings store now self-heals on load: a corrupt `settings.json` is renamed aside to `settings.json.corrupt-<ts>`, a warning is logged, and the app continues with an empty store instead of panicking on `serde_json::from_str`.

Hardened persistence by writing through `OpenOptions` + `write_all` + `sync_all` before the atomic rename, closing the torn-write window on NTFS that previously left the file at the right length but full of NUL bytes after a crash or power loss.

Fatal startup failures on Windows now surface a native `AURA could not start` message box (with macOS/Linux falling back to stderr) that names the data directory, the crash log path, and the settings file users can rename to recover, instead of the previous invisible exit under `windows_subsystem = "windows"`.

Replaced `.expect` calls in the embedded server's ready channel with a `Result`-carrying signal so the main thread can react to startup errors (and `RecvError`) by showing the new dialog and exiting cleanly.

highlights: Invite friends modal in the bottom taskbar
Unified sidekick width across every app
Self-healing recovery for corrupt Windows settings
Release pipeline no longer fails on dropped asset uploads
